item.title: As overseas terrorists regroup, is the Iran war increasing danger in the U.S.?
item.summary: Investigators in the U.S. search for motives in three recent instances of targeted attacks, and whether they are related to the war in Iran.

item.title: Israel and Iran attack gas facilities, in a major escalation that rattles markets
item.summary: President Trump said that Israel acted alone when it struck the South Pars gas field in Iran. Trump threatened Iran to halt its attacks on Qatar's facilities, or face a "blow up" of their South Pars field.

item.title: Gas price spike spurs a political blame game in California
item.summary: California's gas prices have long been high, and spikes due to the war with Iran have sparked debate over who's to blame. Some Democrats say Gov. Gavin Newsom could do more to ease prices.

item.title: Mamdani put Ramadan at the center of NYC's cultural life, bringing joy -- and a backlash
item.summary: NYC Mayor Mamdani observed Ramadan publicly at a time when many politicians and activists on the right are voicing hostility and in some cases open bigotry toward American Muslims.

item.title: Cursive is back. But should students be learning the skill?
item.summary: A Virginia after-school cursive club went viral. More than two dozen states require cursive in their curriculums. Is it an effective learning tool or just nostalgia?

item.title: This tax season, there's a new deduction for interest on car loans
item.summary: Taxpayers who purchased a new vehicle in 2025 may qualify for a new deduction on their taxes — even if they're not itemizing. But not everyone is eligible.

item.title: Kick your tiredness with these 7 natural energy boosters
item.summary: A full calendar doesn't mean you have to feel exhausted all the time. Experts share natural ways to boost energy and beat the constant battle of tiredness.

item.title: It's called 'private credit' — and it could lead to big trouble on Wall Street
item.summary: The risky lending business has been booming — but now its problems are becoming increasingly visible on Wall Street and beyond.

item.title: Cesar Chavez abused and raped women and girls, NYT investigation says
item.summary: A New York Times investigation has revealed allegations that the late renowned labor leader abused girls and raped Dolores Huerta, his longtime organizing partner.

item.title: A mom wrote a kids' book on grief. She was just convicted of her husband's murder
item.summary: A Utah jury convicted Kouri Richins of fatally spiking her husband's drink with fentanyl in 2022. Prosecutors said she was hoping to collect millions of dollars from multiple life insurance policies.
